title: Optimizing Applications

header.html: Apply concurrency concepts (4.3.1); optimize memory and compute power (4.3.2); optimize application messaging (4.3.3); implement caching with AWS services (4.3.4); detect performance bottlenecks (4.3.5); use AWS AI tools to identify optimization opportunities (4.3.6)
the official AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C03) exam guide, Task 4.3

html:
1Concurrency

Control Meaning
Lambda reserved concurrency Guarantees and caps concurrency for one function; protects downstream services
Lambda provisioned concurrency Pre-initialized environments; removes cold starts
EC2 Auto Scaling Adds and removes instances with target tracking or schedules
Connection pooling Reuse database connections; RDS Proxy pools for Lambda
Thread pools Limit parallel work inside an application
Exam tip

. Many Lambda invocations exhaust RDS connections = RDS Proxy. Protect a fragile downstream system = reserved concurrency as a cap.

2Memory and compute

Service Tuning
Lambda More memory = more CPU; test several sizes: a larger size can finish faster and cost the same or less; use a power-tuning approach
EC2 and containers Match instance or task size to CPU- or memory-bound workloads
Code efficiency Reuse SDK clients outside the handler; avoid repeated initialization

3Messaging optimization

Technique Benefit
SQS batching (send and receive up to 10 messages) Fewer requests, lower cost
SQS long polling Fewer empty receives
SNS fan-out to SQS Parallel, independent processing
SNS filter policies Deliver only relevant messages
Lambda batch size and batching window Process more per invocation

4Caching

Cache Reduces
ElastiCache Database reads (any data)
DAX DynamoDB read latency to microseconds
CloudFront Origin load and latency for web and API content
API Gateway cache Backend calls per stage

5Bottlenecks and AI tools

Detect bottlenecks with CloudWatch metrics (latency, errors, throttles, queue depth, CPU), X-Ray (slow downstream calls) and Lambda insights. Typical findings: a single hot partition, not enough concurrency, too small memory, too many small messages, no cache.

AWS AI tools can spot performance bottlenecks, resource waste and code inefficiency [Verify live]; measure before and after every change.

Exam tip

. Measure first, change one thing, measure again. A scenario that shows a metric (high queue depth, throttles, high latency) points to the specific control above.

Exam tip

. RDS connection exhaustion from Lambda = RDS Proxy; slow CPU-bound function = more memory.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Hundreds of concurrent Lambda invocations exhaust an RDS database's connections. What helps most?

  • ALarger Lambda memory only
  • BA bigger S3 bucket
  • CRDS Proxy
  • DA DLQ
Show the answer

Answer: C. RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections.

S2A latency-sensitive Lambda function suffers cold starts. What should the team configure?

  • AA smaller timeout
  • BA DLQ
  • CAn S3 trigger
  • DProvisioned concurrency
Show the answer

Answer: D. Provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm.

S3A Lambda function is CPU-bound and slow. What is the simplest first change?

  • AAdd an environment variable
  • BAdd a layer
  • CRemove its role
  • DIncrease its memory
Show the answer

Answer: D. CPU scales with memory.

S4A function floods a fragile downstream API. How can the team cap it?

  • AA larger batch window
  • BReserved concurrency
  • CA longer retention period
  • DA new alias
Show the answer

Answer: B. Reserved concurrency caps how many copies run.

S5An app sends thousands of single SQS messages and costs are high. What reduces requests?

  • AShorter visibility timeout
  • BA FIFO queue
  • CBatch send and receive
  • DA DLQ
Show the answer

Answer: C. Batching reduces the number of API requests.

S6Repeated DynamoDB reads of the same items need microsecond latency. What fits?

  • ALarger items
  • BDAX
  • CA scan
  • DS3 Lifecycle
Show the answer

Answer: B. DAX caches DynamoDB reads in memory.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does provisioned concurrency remove?

Show the answer

Cold starts.

R2What does reserved concurrency do?

Show the answer

Guarantees and caps a function's concurrency.

R3What gives Lambda more CPU?

Show the answer

More memory.

R4How many messages can SQS batch operations carry?

Show the answer

Up to 10.

R5What pools connections for Lambda and RDS?

Show the answer

RDS Proxy.

R6Name two caching services.

Show the answer

For example ElastiCache and DAX (also CloudFront and API Gateway cache).

7Quick Reference Card

Tuning memory drives CPU; test sizes; reuse clients
Messaging batch (up to 10), long polling, fan-out, filter policies
Caching ElastiCache, DAX, CloudFront, API Gateway
Method measure, change one thing, measure again
